clue.text: "Take prepared rice and add half pear", perhaps

definitions.text: "Take prepared rice and add half pear", perhaps

indicators.note: rice that is prepared is worked into a new form, so its letters are rearranged
half of the word pear keeps only its first two letters

explanation.surface: A cook's instruction for a rice and pear dish.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is the example: RECI (rice rearranged) plus PE (half of pear), and the quoted instruction is itself a typical line from a cookbook.
explanation.definitionFit: A quoted cooking instruction is a sample of the kind of text found in a dish's written method.

clue.text: Rhythmic monologue: I had it with little of your speed

parts.note: rap is rhythmic spoken verse
I had contracts to I'd
taken as written

indicators.note: a little of the word your is just its first letter

explanation.surface: A rapper boasts about how fast they delivered their monologue.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: swiftness or quickness of movement.

clue.text: German poet, not a second Frost in the making here?

indicators.note: not signals that the letter for a second is dropped from the poet's name

parts.note: Friedrich Schiller was a German poet and dramatist
s is the abbreviation for second

explanation.surface: A German poet is contrasted with the American poet Robert Frost.
explanation.walkthrough: Frost looks like the poet Robert Frost, beside Schiller; it is ice, made in a fridge.
explanation.definitionFit: A refrigerating unit is where cold and ice form, so frost is made inside it.

clue.text: What's for turning shepherd's hay and tuning "Shepherd's Hey"?

explanation.surface: A farm tool and a musical device, both serving a shepherd.
explanation.walkthrough: Shepherd's Hey is a folk-dance tune arranged by Percy Grainger; a pitch fork (tuning fork) sets its note.
explanation.definitionFit: A long-pronged farm tool tosses hay, and a tuning fork giving a reference note is also called by this name.

clue.text: Took steps endlessly, having look inside it's essential for flight security

indicators.note: inside places the word for look within the shortened word
endlessly means the last letter of the word for took steps is cut off

parts.note: strode means walked with long steps
air means a look or appearance

explanation.surface: Someone climbing purposefully pauses to inspect the safety of the stairs.
explanation.walkthrough: Flight looks like air travel; here it is a flight of stairs, and a stair rod holds the carpet in place.
explanation.definitionFit: A rod fixing carpet to each step keeps a staircase safe to walk on.

clue.text: To give impressions of their character, these are depressed

definitions.text: To give impressions of their character, these are depressed

parts.words: To give impressions of their character, these are depressed
parts.note: reads like gloomy people revealing their personality; really keys pressed down to print letters, character being a typed symbol

explanation.definitionFit: Keys on an old writing machine are pressed down to strike letters onto paper.

clue.text: Patient's heart treatment's the best possible

indicators.note: the heart of the word patient is its middle letter

parts.note: deal means treatment, as in a fair deal

explanation.surface: A medical report on a patient's heart care being the best available.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: perfect, the best one could hope for.

clue.text: Administration for instance beset by turbulent miner

indicators.note: beset by means surrounded, so the rearranged letters enclose the abbreviation
turbulent means disordered, so the letters of miner are rearranged

parts.note: eg abbreviates exempli gratia, for instance

explanation.surface: Management faced with an unruly coal miner.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turbulent' gives RIMEN; 'Administration' looks like government, but here it is administering a course of treatment.
explanation.definitionFit: A regimen is a prescribed course, as of medicine or diet, i.e. an administering of treatment.

clue.text: Present time in which there's no returning

indicators.note: in which says the reversed piece sits inside the word for time

parts.note: a date is a point in time

indicators.note: returning means the word no is read backwards

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A moment in time from which there is no going back.
explanation.definitionFit: Present as a verb: to give or hand over as a gift.

clue.text: Where your Pekin ducks may be ready to take away?

definitions.text: Where your Pekin ducks may be ready to take away?

parts.words: Where your Pekin ducks may be ready to take away?
parts.note: reads like a takeaway restaurant selling roast duck; really Pekin ducks are fine clothes from China, washed and ready for collection

explanation.definitionFit: A laundry run by Chinese owners is where washed garments await collection.

clue.text: Get some beer while grabbing a redhead at dance — it's full of characters

indicators.note: grabbing means the beer word holds the next letter inside it

parts.note: pints are measures of beer
the head of red is its first letter
a hop is an informal dance

explanation.surface: At a dance, someone buys beer while chatting up a red-haired partner.
explanation.walkthrough: Characters here are printed letters, not lively people.
explanation.definitionFit: A place where printing is done is full of type, each piece a letter or symbol.

clue.text: Importer of stones from the Spanish ruin?

parts.note: el is Spanish for the
gin is known as mother's ruin

explanation.surface: Someone bringing in stones from a Spanish ruined castle.
explanation.walkthrough: Lord Elgin brought the Parthenon (Elgin) Marbles to Britain; 'ruin' is gin through the old nickname mother's ruin.
explanation.definitionFit: A British lord brought ancient marble sculptures from Athens to London.

clue.text: Sea creature slaughter is around record height

indicators.note: is around means the words for kill surround the next pieces

parts.note: do in means kill
LP is a long-playing record

explanation.surface: Slaughter of a marine creature makes record numbers.
explanation.definitionFit: A clever marine mammal of the toothed whale family.

clue.text: Greeting me in spring-time, initially?

parts.note: a well is a spring of water
taken as written

indicators.note: initially takes the first letter of the word time

explanation.surface: A friend greets me in springtime.
explanation.definitionFit: An old-fashioned salutation, said when meeting someone pleasantly.

clue.text: Twisted roots and trunk

indicators.note: twisted means bent out of shape, so the letters of roots are rearranged

explanation.surface: A tree's twisted roots and its trunk.
explanation.definitionFit: The trunk is the main part of a body, without head or limbs.

clue.text: Turn informer about former Prime Minister, showing fury

indicators.note: about means the word for inform goes round the name

parts.note: to sing is slang for informing to the police
Pitt the Elder and the Younger were British Prime Ministers

explanation.surface: Someone turns on an old Prime Minister in anger.
explanation.definitionFit: Spitting mad means furious.

clue.text: Carmen, perhaps, or the Spanish bird turning up with the French?

indicators.note: in a down clue turning up reads the run of words backwards

parts.note: taken as written
el is Spanish for the
a tit is a small songbird
le is French for the

explanation.surface: Is Carmen a Spanish bird or a French one?
explanation.walkthrough: 'turning up' suits a down clue, where reading backwards means reading upward. Carmen is the heroine of Bizet's opera of that name.
explanation.definitionFit: The heroine of an opera named after her plays the part that gives the work its name.

clue.text: Who might supply wee runts running out?

definitions.text: Who might supply wee runts running out?

indicators.note: running out suggests the letters of wee runts fleeing in disorder, so they are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone provides for little runts who are scampering about.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue defines too: a woman who breastfeeds another's babies supplies the wee ones.
explanation.definitionFit: A woman employed to breastfeed another's infants feeds tiny babies.

clue.text: One in Boat Race perhaps is depressed being behind stern of. Oxford vessel

indicators.note: being behind places the word for depressed after the rest
the stern of a boat is its back, so the last letter of Oxford

parts.note: an ark is a vessel
blue means depressed

explanation.surface: A rower in the Boat Race is gloomy, sitting at the back of the boat.
explanation.walkthrough: Dark blue is Oxford's colour in the annual Oxford-Cambridge Boat Race on the Thames.
explanation.definitionFit: Oxford rowers and sportsmen are called by their university colour.

clue.text: Advised of danger, almost everyone took up weapons

indicators.note: almost means the word for everyone loses its last letter

parts.note: all means everyone
armed means equipped with weapons

explanation.surface: Warned of a threat, nearly everyone took up arms.
explanation.definitionFit: Being warned that something threatens one makes one frightened and on guard.

clue.text: Temporary respite until conflict ends, primarily

definitions.text: Temporary respite until conflict ends, primarily

indicators.note: primarily picks the first letter of each of the five words before it

explanation.surface: A pause in fighting until the war is over.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue defines too: a ceasefire is a break in hostilities.
explanation.definitionFit: A ceasefire is an agreed pause in fighting.

clue.text: Hated international organisation did not tell truth about king

parts.note: UN is the United Nations

indicators.note: about means the word for told untruths goes round the next letter

parts.note: lied means told untruths
K is the chess abbreviation for king

explanation.surface: A hated international body lied about a king.
explanation.definitionFit: Disliked, not looked on with favour.

clue.text: Suit well matched to dress, oddly

parts.note: a spa is a mineral spring

indicators.note: oddly takes the first, third and fifth letters of the word dress

explanation.surface: A suit that goes well with a dress, oddly enough.
explanation.definitionFit: One of the four suits in a pack of cards.

clue.text: Overdue in Pyrenean tourist centre from the tableland

indicators.note: in places the word for overdue inside the town

parts.note: Pau is a resort town at the foot of the Pyrenees
late means overdue

explanation.surface: Arriving late at a mountain resort up on high ground.
explanation.definitionFit: An elevated area of flat land.

clue.text: Lifted by a drunken bowler run out?

definitions.text: Lifted by a drunken bowler run out?

indicators.note: drunken means staggering, so the letters left are rearranged
out means the letter for run is dropped

parts.note: r is the cricket abbreviation for run

explanation.surface: A cricket bowler drunk after a run-out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out' removes R from BOWLER leaving BOWLE, which 'drunken' rearranges. 'Lifting the elbow' means drinking heavily.
explanation.definitionFit: Bending the arm to raise a glass is a joint lifted by a heavy drinker.

clue.text: The King, with Merlin perhaps, form the central government

indicators.note: perhaps signals that the letters of Merlin may be given in another order

explanation.surface: King Arthur and Merlin together form a central government.
explanation.walkthrough: The Kremlin is the seat of Russian government in Moscow.
explanation.definitionFit: The Moscow citadel housing Russian power stands for its rulers.

clue.text: Brigade mobilisation limits it!

indicators.note: limits means the two words enclose the letters inside them

explanation.surface: Mobilising a brigade sets limits on standing down.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue defines too: mobilisation stops release from service.
explanation.definitionFit: Release from military service is what a call-up rules out.

clue.text: One employed in light industry

parts.note: reads like a factory hand making small goods; really light means daylight, so someone who works by day

explanation.definitionFit: A person hired by the day, or who works daytime hours.

clue.text: "Swayed" is moved this way!

indicators.note: moved means the letters of the two words are shifted into a new order

explanation.surface: A word is shifted along.
explanation.definitionFit: To one side, describing motion that is lateral.

clue.text: Interfere with sound of gong

indicators.note: sound of means the word for gong is said aloud

parts.note: gong is British slang for a medal

explanation.surface: Someone messes with the noise a gong makes.
explanation.definitionFit: To meddle is to intrude in others' affairs.
